The child who knows they're sorry but can't say it

When they break a friend's toy or make a mistake, a child knows they're sorry — yet can't easily get the words out. Out of embarrassment, they might even whirl around and turn their back.

In moments like these, pressing them with "Say sorry, quick!" only makes a child shrink further. An apology doesn't come out of pressure — it comes only when a child finds their courage.

Curious about the plot of this apology story? Explore the lesson of the apology story alongside its illustrations. Meet the key scenes of the story, too. content.alt: 31. One Little Sorry Makes Your Heart Fluffy! - An apology takes courage
content.text:
An apology takes courage

An apology isn't about 'losing' — it's the 'courage to mend a relationship.' But for a child, saying sorry takes more courage than you might think.

An unspoken apology weighs on a child like a heavy stone pressing on their chest. On the other hand, when they find the courage to apologize and experience a relationship being restored, a child learns that apologizing is a good thing — and next time, they can say sorry more easily.

content.alt: 31. One Little Sorry Makes Your Heart Fluffy! - Hori's brave little word
content.text:
Hori's brave little word

In the story One Little Sorry Makes Your Heart Fluffy!, Hori knocks down Toto's block tower but is too embarrassed to apologize. That's when Toto reaches out first, saying, "I want to play with you."

Hori gathers his courage, takes a deep breath, and looks Toto in the eyes. "Toto, I'm sorry I knocked down your tower!" In that instant, the heavy stone pressing on his chest turns into fluffy cotton candy.

content.alt: 31. One Little Sorry Makes Your Heart Fluffy! - Growing the courage to apologize together at home
content.text:
Growing the courage to apologize together at home

After reading the book, when your child does something wrong, try reading their heart first — instead of "Say sorry, quick," say "You were sorry, but the words wouldn't come out, huh?" A child whose shyness is understood finds the courage to apologize sincerely.

Above all, let your child see you say "I'm sorry" first. An adult's heartfelt apology is the best example a child can have.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions

Q. How do I teach my child to apologize?

A. Show them through a story that one little "sorry" makes the heart fluffy. Rather than forcing it, it's better to let them feel that an apology makes a relationship warm again.

Q. Can an apology story help?

A. By watching the main character apologize sincerely and make up, your child learns how to express a sorry heart, too. Apology stories show that saying sorry is nothing to be ashamed of.

Q. My child is shy about apologizing or finds it hard.

A. Rather than scolding the mistake, explain how good it feels to put a sorry heart into words. When you praise them for finding the courage to apologize, they'll do it on their own next time.
